doc.title: Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG Tier List
doc.summary: The Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG tier list, updated November 6, 2026: Angelechy holds Tier 1 alone. Ranked from 123,146 YGO Omega ladder games.

blocks.md: This Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG tier list ranks the decks on the YGO Omega TCG ladder by expected win rate, from ranked games through November 6, 2026. **Angelechy** holds Tier 1 alone, with an expected 54.0% win rate and 13.3% of the meta.

blocks.title: What this list can't tell you
blocks.md: We rank TCG decks from ranked YGO Omega games in the Gold+ band, set by each pair's average rating. We adjust for rating gaps and turn order. Specialist pilots, deck choices and anything the game log doesn't record can still move a deck's number, and tournament fields can differ from the ladder.

blocks.caption: TCG tiers for November 6, 2026: Angelechy leads at 54.0% expected win rate. Tier 4 shows its top five builds; Others counts the rest.

blocks.md: A deck's tier says how many points of expected win rate it gives up to the leader. For what moved this week, read the [latest meta report](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-meta-report-november-6-2026). For the other ladder, see the [Genesys tier list](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-genesys-tier-list), and between updates, the [live statistics page](/statistics).

blocks.text: Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG tier list at a glance

blocks.md:

The TCG ladder is 19 days into the 10.2026 season, with 123,146 games from 6,833 players. The most played deck, Angelechy, holds 13.3% of the meta. The 18 builds shown below cover 65% of it. We show Tiers 1–3 and the five highest-ranked Tier 4 builds; the [statistics page](/statistics) lists the rest.

| [**Angelechy**](/statistics/archetypes/482?ladder=tcg) | **54.0%** | Leader | 52.6–55.3 | 13.3% | 924 |

blocks.text: Which decks are underplayed and overplayed?

blocks.md:
The underplayed decks reach Tier 2 or better on a small share of the meta. Specialists may pilot most of their games, so test one before you trust its number. The overplayed decks sit among the ten most played and land in Tier 3 or lower.

- **Underplayed:** Branded / Dracotail (1.2% of the meta, expected 51.3%), Maliss / @Ignister (1.6% of the meta, expected 51.5%) and Power Patron / Ars Magna / Light and Darkness Ritual (1.9% of the meta, expected 52.3%)
- **Overplayed:** HERO (6.5% of the meta, expected 50.6%), Dark Time Wizard / K9 (2.5% of the meta, expected 49.3%) and Invoked (2.3% of the meta, expected 49.1%)

We show matchups that outperform or underperform the model's expectation for the six highest-ranked builds against Tiers 1–3. We require a 95% interval clear of that expectation and at least 300 games. An above-expected matchup can still have a win rate below 50%.

| Deck | Above expectation | Below expectation |
|---|---|---|
| **Angelechy** | **[Power Patron / Ars Magna / Artmage, 54.2% (2,470 games)]{#4fdc8c}** | **[Blitzclique, 47.7% (1,624 games)]{#ff8594}** |
| **Elfnote / Power Patron / Ars Magna** | None clear | None clear |
| **Radiant Typhoon** | **[Angelechy, 52.2% (1,228 games)]{#4fdc8c}** | None clear |
| **Power Patron / Ars Magna / Artmage** | None clear | **[Angelechy, 45.8% (2,470 games)]{#ff8594}** |
| **Power Patron / Ars Magna / Light and Darkness Ritual** | None clear | None clear |
| **Blitzclique** | **[Angelechy, 52.3% (1,624 games)]{#4fdc8c}** | **[HERO, 45.0% (705 games)]{#ff8594}** |

Every number comes from ranked games on [YGO Omega](/wiki/ygo-omega-wiki), the same data as the [statistics page](/statistics). Below are the settings behind this week's TCG list. The [statistics methodology](/wiki/ygo-omega-statistics-methodology) explains the model and why we replaced the old ranking score.

We fit the model on Gold+ games. A game's band comes from the average of both players' previous-day ratings, each capped at 3,000, so a Gold+ game can include one player below Gold. Both players need 5 ranked games this season, or we leave the game out. Decklists need no minimum number of games. A deck needs 30 deck-games for its own estimate and a row; smaller decks share one pooled estimate and stay off the list. So far this season, these rules removed 4,978 games for player activity and 74,255 in the Iron band, where the pair averages under Bronze or one side has no rating, out of 469,858 games.

blocks.text: How a deck gets its number

blocks.md: For each decisive game, we fit both deck strengths, the going-first effect and the rating-gap effect. Expected win rate is a deck's predicted result against the field, weighted by meta share, with equal ratings and no first-turn edge. Decks with little evidence shrink toward the ladder mean.

The deck with the best expected win rate leads. Every other deck takes its tier from how many points it sits under the leader:

| Tier | Points under the leader |
|---|---|
| Tier 1 | The leader, plus the next deck within 0.5 |
| Tier 1.5 | Within 0.5, once Tier 1 is full |
| Tier 2 | Up to 3 |
| Tier 3 | Up to 4.5 |
| Tier 4 | More than 4.5 |

Tier 1 holds two decks at most. When the leader's rate moves, the boundaries move with it, so a deck can change tier in a week its own rate held still. A deck needs 1% of the meta and 25 different players before it gets a tier. The model already corrects for small samples; the player floor keeps out decks that a few specialists carry.

- **Meta share** is a deck's share of deck-games. Each game counts once per player, mirrors included.
- **Raw win rate** is wins divided by wins, losses and draws. Draws stay in the denominator, games without a result stay out of rates, and the strength fit skips draws.
- **Mirrors** count toward meta share and help estimate the rating and turn-order effects. Raw win rates and matchups leave them out.
- **The 95% interval** shows the uncertainty around expected win rate. We widen it when daily results swing more than sampling noise explains.
- **Decks** take up to 2 archetype names, lead archetype first. A card in at least 10% of decklists counts as a staple, and names no deck, when 50% or more of the lists running it hold no other card of its archetype. We merge equivalent hybrid orders into one key and keep hybrids apart from pure builds.

items.q: What is the best Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG deck right now?
items.md: Angelechy, with an expected 54.0% win rate (95% interval 52.6–55.3) at 13.3% of the meta, from ladder games through November 6, 2026.

items.q: What are the Tier 1 decks in TCG?
What is the most played deck in the TCG meta?
items.md: Angelechy, at 13.3% of the meta. It has an expected 54.0% win rate and leads the tier list too.

By distance from the leader in expected win rate. Tier 1 is the leader plus one deck within 0.5 points; further decks within that gap go to Tier 1.5. Tier 2 reaches 3 points under the leader and Tier 3 reaches 4.5; Tier 4 takes the rest. A deck needs 1% of the meta and 25 different players to be ranked.

items.q: Why did a deck change tier when its win rate barely moved?
items.md: The tiers count from the leader. When the leader's expected win rate rises or falls, every tier boundary moves with it, and decks near a boundary cross it.

items.q: Is this tier list based on tournament results?
items.md: No. It uses ranked games on YGO Omega. Tournament players can face a different field, so treat the list as a ladder benchmark.

items.q: Does a popular deck get a higher tier?
items.md: No. HERO holds 6.5% of the meta and sits in Tier 3. Branded / Dracotail holds 1.2% and sits in Tier 2.

items.q: How much does going first matter?
items.md: The model estimates a 57.2% win probability going first between equal decks and player ratings on the TCG ladder. This coefficient uses the games in the fit, including post-side games.

items.q: How often is the tier list updated?
items.md: Every week, on this same page. Each week also gets its own [meta report](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-meta-report-november-6-2026), and the [statistics page](/statistics) shows the current numbers between updates.

items.q: Where can I see decklists for these decks?
items.md: The [statistics page](/statistics) has sample decklists, card usage and full matchup tables for each deck.
